svg.title: Encryption at rest: envelope v2 write and fail-closed read
svg.desc: The encrypting adapter around the WORM object store. Writes produce a v2 envelope whose AES-GCM associated data is the object key. Reads refuse plaintext unless it is chain-log data, globally allowed, or pinned in a digest-checked legacy inventory; strict mode also refuses unbound v1 envelopes. Step 1: put_object first checks the caller's SHA-256 over the plaintext, so a CAS mismatch fails before any cryptography runs. Step 2: encrypt_blob makes a fresh 256-bit DEK and 96-bit nonce and seals with AES-256-GCM, authenticating the object key as associated data. Step 3: The KEK wraps the DEK; the envelope JSON is WORM-written and hashed as ciphertext, so integrity checks never need the key. Step 4: On read, bytes that are not an envelope are refused unless chain-log data, globally allowed, or pinned by the legacy inventory. Step 5: Strict mode refuses an unbound v1 envelope that the inventory does not pin, before any key is unwrapped. Step 6: decrypt_blob refuses a shredded envelope, checks the ciphertext hash, then unwraps the DEK; each failure has a named error. Step 7: AES-GCM opens with the key being read as associated data; an envelope copied to another key fails with BlobAuthenticationError.

Object capsule store, opt-in (ADR-0185, ADR-0290, ADR-0295; experimental)

legacy inventory loaded once; missing, malformed or pin-mismatched ⇒ refuse to start

On read, bytes that are not an envelope are refused unless chain-log data, globally allowed, or pinned by the legacy inventory.
Strict mode refuses an unbound v1 envelope that the inventory does not pin, before any key is unwrapped.
